channel.title: The Lowndes Signal - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Lowndes Signal (lowndessignal.com)

item.title: Faith Community Calendar
item.description: Upcoming faith events in Lowndes County: prayer nights, Valentine’s banquet, Black History Month program, wild game supper, plus how to submit your church activities.

item.title: Beulah congregation blesses Calhoun track program
item.description: Beulah Primitive Baptist Church continues its annual support of The Calhoun School, donating $1,260 to the track and field team during a joint worship service.

item.title: When fitness meets fame
item.description: A gymgoer keeps ending up in a TikTok guy’s workout videos. Amy advises skipping the silent resentment, asking him to angle the camera away, or enlisting gym staff for help.

item.title: How small businesses in Alabama can use social media in 2026
item.description: Alabama small businesses that want to grow have to show up where customers already spend their attention.

item.title: Mosses residents question chief's fitness for office
item.description: At a Mosses town meeting, interim police chief Kelvin Mitchell denied ties to a murder suspect and missing guns as residents and a victim’s family questioned his fitness to lead.

item.title: Governor opens summer internship applications
item.description: Gov. Kay Ivey opens applications for a nine-week Governor’s Office summer internship in Montgomery for college students, running June 2 – July 31; deadline to apply is March 13.

item.title: Sanders voted 20th athlete contest winner
item.description: AaLyria Sanders, a Calhoun School senior cheerleader and dancer, wins Lowndes County Athlete of the Week with 46% of votes and advances to April’s Athlete of the Year contest.

item.title: Lowndes County Arrests Jan. 23 - 31
item.description: Lowndes County reports arrests from Jan. 23 - 29, including domestic violence, harassment, probation revocation, SORNA violations and traffic-related offenses.

item.title: Faith Community Calendar
item.description: Local churches share February and March events, including chili cook-off, Valentine banquet, Black History program and wild game supper, plus details on submitting items to the Faith Calendar.

item.title: Fort Deposit officials take oath of office
item.description: After a contentious election, Fort Deposit swears in Mayor Madelene Means and town council, pledging unity, new ideas and regular town halls to shape the town's future.
